data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is a category mistake: Popper conflates the logical status of a theory (unproven) with the psychological/biological necessity of acting, creating a false dilemma between induction and arbitrariness.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If Popper claims his methodology dictates rational action, not just theory generation, this separation is invalid.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'biological imperative' is just a naturalized form of induction (expecting survival based on past fitness), the problem remains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'preference' influences which experiments are funded or which risks are taken, it functions logically as a probability assignment regardless of the label.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism here is biological pragmatism. Humans must act; waiting for logical certainty is impossible. The 'preference' is not a logical derivation but a biological imperative to use the most robust tool available. It is defensible on Popper's terms only if we admit that his logic applies to the growth of knowledge (theories), while his advice on action belongs to the domain of biology/psychology. The 'smuggling' is only apparent if one demands logic to dictate all action. The cost is the separation of epistemology from praxis.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
